ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the curve of function g rises from the lower left toward the upper right; near point a it is still upward but gradually becomes flatter; near point b the curve is relatively gentle, and afterward it starts to become steeper to the right; point c is on the steep rising branch on the left; point d is on the right branch, where the curve descends to the right. Reasoning: g'(x) being positive means the graph of the function is rising near that point; g'(x) decreasing means the tangent slope becomes smaller as x increases, that is, locally it is concave down and becoming flatter. Near point a, the curve is rising and the slope becomes smaller, so it satisfies g'(x) positive and decreasing. Point d has a negative slope, the slope at point c is increasing, and point b does not fit this condition as well as a. Therefore the answer is a.

raw_record.question_text: The graph of a function g is shown above. Which labeled point on the graph is where g'(x) is positive and decreasing?

method.method_draft: First read the graph: the labeled point a lies on the left rising part of the curve where the function is increasing but flattening out as x moves right; b is on a nearly flat portion before the curve begins to steepen; c is on a steep rising part; d is on the right branch where the curve is decreasing. From the text, the target condition is that g'(x) is positive and decreasing. Use the bridge that g'(x) positive means the graph is increasing, and g'(x) decreasing means the slopes of tangent lines are getting smaller, equivalently the graph is concave down locally. Point a is on an increasing, concave-down segment, so the answer is a.
